sections.title: Editorial
sections.summary: Mid‑2020s update: tariffs announced on “Liberation Day” accelerated a shift to a multipolar world; the US reverted to fiscal spending, while Germany’s fiscal/defence pivot lifted confidence; Chart 1 shows decade‑to‑date returns across major assets.

sections.title: Historical secular trends
sections.summary: Overview of decade‑by‑decade structural forces and rotating market leadership; Chart 2 maps events, regimes, and winning assets from the 1960s to the 2020s.

subsections.title: Multipolarity and strategic reshoring
subsections.summary: Global fragmentation intensified; US tariff push raised recession fears but evolved into bilateral, security‑focused trade deals; reshoring, not broad deglobalisation; Chinese exports redirected regionally (Chart 3).

subsections.title: Interest rate normalisation
subsections.summary: Fed cut rates to 3.75–4% by Nov 2025; 10‑year UST near 4%; private balance‑sheet strength supports resilience; public‑debt burdens keep debt‑sustainability central to policy.

subsections.title: Innovation super cycle
subsections.summary: AI‑led capex surge with energy/grid capacity as binding constraint; benefits are large but uncertain; broader innovation spans energy, storage, and life sciences.

subsections.title: China’s balance sheet recession
subsections.summary: Weak consumer confidence and high savings reflect real‑estate shock; policy moves aim to engineer a managed, sustainable equity bull market to repair household balance sheets (Chart 6).

subsections.title: Private sector balance sheets
subsections.summary: US households and many corporates exhibit balance‑sheet strength post‑GFC; higher rates have even aided some large‑cap net interest income; public sector weakened.

subsections.title: India and China
subsections.summary: India: domestic‑demand‑driven (~60% of GDP) with strong equity outperformance; China: re‑entry justified by policy shifts and rising self‑sufficiency; risks (e.g., Taiwan) seen as diminished under current US stance (Chart 8/9).

subsections.title: Gold and digital assets (out‑of‑system assets)
subsections.summary: Gold reached new nominal highs (breached USD 4,000/oz in Oct 2025); strength tied to weak public balance sheets and weaponisation of the financial system, spurring structural demand, notably from non‑Western investors (Chart 10).

subsections.title: CHF: Swiss assets as a store of value
subsections.summary: Store‑of‑value markets (notably Switzerland) offer protection via strong institutions and low public debt; equities skew defensive and favor active management; CHF’s safe‑haven role enhances diversification (Charts 11–12).

sections.title: Key risk factors
sections.summary: Interlinked risks: climate, cyber, dormant systemic risks (shadow banking/private credit), geopolitics, and infrastructure vulnerabilities.
